knowledge:
- key_parameters: smoothfunc=The smoothing algorithm to use ("lawsglad" for AWS or "haarseg" for HaarSeg) ;; lambdabreak=Penalty parameter for breakpoint detection (decreasing it identifies more breakpoints) ;; lambdacluster=Penalty parameter for clustering within chromosomes ;; lambdaclusterGen=Penalty parameter for clustering over the whole genome ;; param=Parameter vector, e.g., c(d=6) (decreasing d to 3 or less is recommended for arrays with low signal-to-noise ratio) ;; genomestep=Logical in daglad; if TRUE, performs a genome-wide smoothing step to identify the normal level ;; deltaN=Threshold to define the normal region interval in daglad ;; forceGL=Thresholds to force gain and loss status assignment in daglad
- alternatives: daglad is an improved version of the original glad function and is recommended for most analyses. smoothfunc="haarseg" is recommended as a faster alternative to "lawsglad" for high-throughput or fast computation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have array CGH log-ratio data and need to identify genomic breakpoints, segment the genome, call copy number alterations (gains, losses, amplicons, deletions), and visualize the genomic profiles.
- pitfalls: For array experiments with very small signal-to-noise ratios, default parameters may fail to detect breakpoints; users must manually decrease the param value (e.g., d=3 or less). Input data frames for as.profileCGH must strictly contain the compulsory columns LogRatio, Chromosome, and PosOrder.

workflows.name: glad_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect genomic breakpoints and assign copy number status using the classic GLAD algorithm.
input: user_data.txt (a data frame containing LogRatio, Chromosome, PosOrder, and optionally PosBase and Clone)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert data to a profileCGH object ;; 2. Run the glad segmentation and calling algorithm ;; 3. Plot the genomic profile with cytoband information
workflows.code:
data(snijders)

profileCGH <- as.profileCGH(gm13330)

res <- glad(profileCGH, mediancenter=FALSE,
                smoothfunc="lawsglad", bandwidth=10, round=1.5,
                model="Gaussian", lkern="Exponential", qlambda=0.999,
                base=FALSE,
                lambdabreak=8, lambdacluster=8, lambdaclusterGen=40,
                type="tricubic", param=c(d=6),
                alpha=0.001, msize=2,
                method="centroid", nmax=8,
                verbose=FALSE)
data(cytoband)
plotProfile(res, unit=3, Bkp=TRUE, labels=FALSE, plotband=FALSE, Smoothing="Smoothing", cytoband = cytoband)

workflows.name: daglad_analysis
workflows.intent: Detect genomic breakpoints and assign copy number status using the improved DAGLAD algorithm with explicit calling thresholds.
input: user_data.txt (a data frame containing LogRatio, Chromosome, PosOrder, and optionally PosBase and Clone)
workflows.stages: 1. Convert data to a profileCGH object ;; 2. Run the daglad segmentation and calling algorithm with custom thresholds ;; 3. Plot the genomic profile with threshold lines
workflows.code:
data(veltman)

profileCGH <- as.profileCGH(P9)

profileCGH <- daglad(profileCGH, mediancenter=FALSE, normalrefcenter=FALSE, genomestep=FALSE,
                     smoothfunc="lawsglad", lkern="Exponential", model="Gaussian",
                     qlambda=0.999,  bandwidth=10, base=FALSE, round=1.5,
                     lambdabreak=8, lambdaclusterGen=40, param=c(d=6), alpha=0.001, msize=2,
                     method="centroid", nmin=1, nmax=8,
                     amplicon=1, deletion=-5, deltaN=0.2,  forceGL=c(-0.3,0.3), nbsigma=3,
                     MinBkpWeight=0.35, CheckBkpPos=TRUE)
plotProfile(profileCGH, Smoothing="Smoothing", Bkp=TRUE, plotband=FALSE, cytoband = cytoband)
abline(h=c(-0.3,-0.2,0.2,0.3),col=c("green","black","black","red"))
axis(2,at=c(-0.3,-0.2,0.2,0.3), labels=c("forceGL[1]","-deltaN","+deltaN","forceGL[2]"), las=2)

workflows.name: array_spatial_visualization
workflows.intent: Visualize spatial layout and raw intensity values of CGH microarrays to detect experimental artifacts.
input: raw_array_data.txt (a table containing Col and Row coordinates and Log2 ratios)
workflows.stages: 1. Create an arrayCGH object from a list containing arrayValues and arrayDesign ;; 2. Plot the spatial layout ;; 3. Plot the 3D perspective layout
workflows.code:
data(arrayCGH)

# object of class arrayCGH

array <- list(arrayValues=array2, arrayDesign=c(4,4,21,22))
class(array) <- "arrayCGH"
arrayPlot(array,"Log2Rat", bar="none")
arrayPersp(array,"Log2Rat", box=FALSE, theta=110, phi=40, bar=FALSE)
